title: Glossary
markdown:
Every term from the course, in alphabetical order. The lesson that introduces each one is in brackets.

| Term | Meaning |
|---|---|
| **__init_subclass__** | A class method that runs each time the class is subclassed. (7.03) |
| **__match_args__** | The attribute order a class pattern uses for positional sub-patterns. (7.04) |
| **__slots__** | A fixed list of attribute names that replaces an object's attribute dictionary. (7.03) |
| **Abstract base class** | A class that only describes methods subclasses must provide; it cannot be instantiated. (4.03) |
| **Argument** | A value passed to a function when it is called. (3.01) |
| **Attribute** | A value stored on an object, reached with a dot: `account.owner`. (4.01) |
| **await** | Pauses a coroutine until the awaited thing finishes, letting others run meanwhile. (7.06) |
| **Bytecode** | The compact form the interpreter turns source code into before running it. (1.01) |
| **Class** | A description of a kind of object: its data and its methods. (4.01) |
| **Closure** | A function together with variables from an enclosing function that it still uses. (3.03) |
| **Comprehension** | An expression that builds a list, dict or set from an iterable: `[x * x for x in xs]`. (5.01) |
| **Context manager** | An object with `__enter__` and `__exit__`, used in a `with` block so cleanup always happens. (7.02) |
| **contextmanager** | The `contextlib` decorator that turns a one-`yield` generator into a context manager. (7.02) |
| **Coroutine** | What calling an `async def` function returns; it runs when awaited. (7.06) |
| **CSV** | Comma-separated values: a text format for tables. (6.02) |
| **Dataclass** | A class whose `__init__`, `__repr__` and `__eq__` are generated from annotated fields. (4.04) |
| **Decorator** | A `@name` line above a function or class that wraps or registers it: `@property`, `@dataclass`. (4.01) |
| **Descriptor** | An object in a class that controls getting and setting an attribute with `__get__` and `__set__`. (7.03) |
| **Dictionary** | A mapping from keys to values with fast lookup. (2.05) |
| **Docstring** | The string right after a `def` or `class` line, describing it. (3.01) |
| **Duck typing** | Using any object that has the needed methods, whatever its class. (4.03) |
| **Dunder method** | A special method such as `__len__` that Python calls for built-in syntax. (4.02) |
| **Dynamic typing** | Values have types, names do not; a name can refer to values of any type. (1.02) |
| **Encoding** | Turning text into bytes (and decoding: back again); UTF-8 is the usual choice (8.04) |
| **Enum** | A fixed set of named values. (4.04) |
| **Event loop** | The asyncio scheduler that runs another task while one is waiting. (7.06) |
| **Exception** | An object raised when something goes wrong; it stops the program unless handled. (4.05) |
| **ExitStack** | A context manager that collects any number of other context managers and closes them all. (7.02) |
| **f-string** | A string with `f` before it, where `{expressions}` are inserted and formatted. (1.03) |
| **Falsy / truthy** | Counting as false (0, "", None, empty collections) or true in a condition. (1.02) |
| **Fixture** | Set-up shared by tests; in pytest a function whose result is passed to tests by name (8.02) |
| **functools.wraps** | A decorator for wrappers that copies the wrapped function's name and docstring. (7.01) |
| **Future** | A placeholder for a result that a pool will produce later; `.result()` waits for it. (7.05) |
| **Generator** | A function with `yield` that produces values one at a time, on demand. (5.02) |
| **GIL** | The global interpreter lock: only one thread runs Python code at a time in CPython. (7.05) |
| **Guard** | An `if` condition after a `case` pattern. (7.04) |
| **Handler** | The part of logging that decides where messages go: the screen, a file, or anything else (8.01) |
| **Immutable** | Cannot be changed after creation: strings, tuples, numbers, frozen dataclasses. (2.01) |
| **Inheritance** | A class taking the attributes and methods of a base class. (4.03) |
| **Interpreter** | The program that reads and runs Python code directly. (1.01) |
| **Iterable / iterator** | Something you can loop over / the object that produces its items one at a time. (5.02) |
| **JSON** | A text format for nested data: objects, arrays, strings, numbers, true, false, null. (6.02) |
| **Key function** | A function passed as `key=` that decides how items are compared when sorting. (5.03) |
| **Keyword argument** | An argument passed by name: `greet(name="Ada")`. (3.02) |
| **Lambda** | A small anonymous function written as an expression. (3.03) |
| **List** | An ordered, changeable sequence. (2.02) |
| **Literal type** | A type hint that allows only certain exact values, like Literal['r', 'w'] (8.03) |
| **Lock** | An object that lets one thread at a time into a section of code. (7.05) |
| **Log level** | How serious a log message is: DEBUG, INFO, WARNING, ERROR or CRITICAL (8.01) |
| **Logger** | A named object from logging.getLogger that sends messages with a level; names form a tree split by dots (8.01) |
| **memoryview** | A view of part of a bytes-like object without copying it (8.04) |
| **Metaclass** | The class of a class; `type` by default. (7.03) |
| **Method** | A function defined in a class and called on an instance. (4.01) |
| **Mock** | An object from unittest.mock that accepts any call, returns what you tell it and remembers how it was used (8.02) |
| **Module** | A `.py` file whose names can be imported. (3.04) |
| **Mutable** | Can be changed in place: lists, dictionaries, sets, most objects. (2.02) |
| **Package** | A folder of modules. (3.04) |
| **Parameter** | A name in a function's definition that receives an argument. (3.01) |
| **Patch** | Temporarily replacing a name with a mock during a test, with unittest.mock.patch (8.02) |
| **Pattern** | The shape after `case`, which a value must have for that case to run. (7.04) |
| **PEP 8** | Python's style guide: naming, spacing, layout. (1.02) |
| **pip** | The tool that installs packages from PyPI. (3.04) |
| **Process** | A separate running program with its own memory; processes can calculate in parallel. (7.05) |
| **Property** | A method used like an attribute, for controlled reading (and writing). (4.01) |
| **Protocol** | A description of the methods an object needs, for type checkers. (5.05) |
| **pyproject.toml** | The file that describes a Python project, its dependencies and its tools (8.06) |
| **Race condition** | A bug where threads change shared data at the same time and a change is lost. (7.05) |
| **Regular expression** | A pattern that describes text to search for or extract. (6.01) |
| **REPL** | The interactive prompt that runs one line at a time and shows results. (1.01) |
| **Scope** | Where a name is visible: local, enclosing, global, built-in (LEGB). (3.03) |
| **Semaphore** | A counter that lets at most N tasks or threads through at once. (7.06) |
| **Set** | An unordered collection of unique values with fast membership tests. (2.05) |
| **Slice** | A part of a sequence: `xs[start:stop:step]`. (2.01) |
| **SQL injection** | A bug where text from a user becomes part of an SQL command; prevented with ? placeholders (8.05) |
| **struct** | The module that packs numbers into bytes and unpacks them, by a format string such as '<HI' (8.04) |
| **TaskGroup** | An `async with` block that starts tasks and waits for all of them. (7.06) |
| **Test case** | A class of tests in unittest; each method starting with test is one test (8.02) |
| **Thread** | A separate line of execution in the same program, sharing its memory. (7.05) |
| **Traceback** | The report printed for an unhandled exception, read from the bottom. (4.05) |
| **Transaction** | A group of database changes saved together with commit or undone together with rollback (8.05) |
| **Tuple** | A fixed, unchangeable sequence for values that belong together. (2.04) |
| **Type hint** | An annotation such as `-> int` that tools use to check types. (5.05) |
| **Type parameter** | A placeholder for a type in a generic function or class, written def f[T](...) (8.03) |
| **TypedDict** | A type hint for a dictionary with known keys and value types (8.03) |
| **Unpacking** | Assigning the items of a sequence to several names at once. (2.04) |
| **Virtual environment** | A folder with its own Python packages for one project. (3.04) |
| **Wheel** | A built Python package file (.whl) that pip installs (8.06) |
